title: From pink to brown: Interaction-driven noise color shift in the Aubry-Andr{é} Model
authors: M. Jiménez-Valdez, S. A. Montes-Camacho, E. J. Torres-Herrera
abstract: We revisit the metal-insulator transition in a one-dimensional lattice subjected to an on-site quasiperiodic potential, modeled using spin-1/2 particles with tunable nearest-neighbor interactions. To characterize the transition, we examine the power-spectrum, defined as the squared modulus of the Fourier transform of consecutive level spacings. In the absence of interactions, the power-spectrum fails to capture clear signatures of the transition, consistently exhibiting brown-noise-like behavior across regimes. In contrast, the interacting case reveals a marked change: the metallic phase displays spectral fluctuations consistent with pink noise, while the insulating phase is characterized by brown noise. These results are supported by analyses of the level spacing distribution and the level number variance. Additionally, we demonstrate that both statistics and the structure of energy eigenstates provide reliable indicators of the transition, in both interacting and non-interacting scenarios.
summary: This work investigates the metal-insulator transition in an interacting spin model on a quasiperiodically modulated lattice. By analyzing the power spectrum of energy level fluctuations, the authors demonstrate that interactions induce a distinct spectral signature: pink noise characterizes the metallic phase, while brown noise marks the insulating phase. This confirms the utility of advanced spectral diagnostics beyond standard measures.
main_problem: The study revisits the metal-insulator transition in a one-dimensional lattice subjected to an on-site quasiperiodic potential.
main_result: Introducing nearest-neighbor interactions causes the power spectrum of energy level fluctuations to shift from brown noise (insulating) to pink noise (metallic), providing a clear diagnostic tool for the transition.
method: The analysis utilizes spectral diagnostics, specifically examining the power-spectrum ($P_k$) of consecutive energy level spacings ($\delta_n$), alongside level spacing distributions and level number variance.
model_or_system: The system is modeled using spin-1/2 particles on a 1D lattice with an on-site quasiperiodic potential, described by a Hamiltonian involving nearest-neighbor interactions. The Aubry-André model serves as the primary framework.
key_observables: Power-spectrum ($P_k$), level spacing distribution ($P(s)$), and level number variance ($\Sigma^2(\ell)$).
important_parameters: Potential strength parameter $h$, interaction strength (tunable nearest-neighbor interactions), and the quasiperiodic potential parameter $ eta$ (inverse golden mean).
main_assumptions: The analysis focuses on the symmetry sector with $S_z = 0$. The power-spectrum approach is emphasized for its ability to distinguish phases where standard indicators might fail.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the metal-insulator transition scheme, comparing non-interacting vs. interacting cases; they also show level spacing distributions and participation ratios across different potential strengths ($h$).
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes spectral fluctuations using multiple diagnostics (power spectrum, level statistics) to characterize the phase transition in both non-interacting and interacting regimes of the AA model.
why_interesting: The use of noise color analysis (pink vs. brown noise) provides a powerful, quantitative signature for distinguishing between metallic/extended and insulating/localized phases in 1D quantum systems, which is relevant to understanding transport in disordered or quasiperiodic media.
